definition: Description of the U.S. as a country built by people who came from all over the world
example: From the Pilgrims to today, waves of immigrants have shaped American culture and identity

definition: National holiday celebrated on the fourth Thursday of November, giving thanks for blessings
example: Thanksgiving has been a national holiday since President Lincoln proclaimed it in 1863

definition: The belief that through hard work, anyone can achieve success and prosperity in the U.S.
example: Many immigrants come to America in pursuit of the American Dream

definition: Latin for 'Out of many, one' — the original U.S. motto representing unity from diversity
example: E Pluribus Unum appears on the Great Seal and on U.S. coins

definition: Monument in Washington D.C. honoring President Abraham Lincoln
example: Martin Luther King Jr. gave his 'I Have a Dream' speech at the Lincoln Memorial in 1963

definition: Tall obelisk in Washington D.C. honoring the first President, George Washington
example: At 555 feet tall, the Washington Monument was the world's tallest structure when completed

definition: The official residence and primary workplace of the President of the United States
example: Every U.S. President since John Adams has lived in the White House

definition: The capital of the United States, home to all three branches of the federal government
example: The White House, Capitol Building, and Supreme Court are all in Washington D.C.

definition: Mountain range running along the eastern United States
example: The Appalachian Trail stretches from Georgia to Maine through the Appalachian Mountains

definition: The world's largest freshwater lake system, located along the U.S.-Canada border
example: The five Great Lakes are Superior, Michigan, Huron, Erie, and Ontario

definition: The first U.S. national park, established in 1872, known for geysers and wildlife
example: Old Faithful in Yellowstone is a famous geyser that erupts regularly

definition: A massive canyon in Arizona carved by the Colorado River, a famous national park
example: The Grand Canyon is over a mile deep and was formed over millions of years

definition: Major mountain range running through the western United States
example: The Rocky Mountains include peaks in Colorado, Montana, and Wyoming

definition: One of the two longest rivers in the U.S., running through the center of the country
example: The Mississippi River flows from Minnesota to the Gulf of Mexico

definition: The ocean bordering the West Coast of the United States
example: Los Angeles, Seattle, and San Francisco are on the Pacific Coast

definition: The ocean bordering the East Coast of the United States
example: New York, Miami, and Boston are on the Atlantic Coast

definition: The United States is made up of 50 states, each with its own government
example: Alaska and Hawaii were the last states added, both in 1959

definition: National flag with 13 stripes (original colonies) and 50 stars (one per state)
example: The 50 stars represent the 50 states; a new star was added when Hawaii joined in 1960

definition: Historic bell in Philadelphia that symbolizes American independence and freedom
example: The Liberty Bell is displayed at Independence Hall in Philadelphia

definition: Monument in New York Harbor symbolizing freedom and opportunity, gifted by France in 1886
example: The Statue of Liberty welcomed millions of immigrants arriving by ship

definition: National bird of the United States, symbolizing strength, courage, and independence
example: The Bald Eagle appears on the Great Seal and is protected by federal law

definition: Official symbol of the United States, featuring a bald eagle with an olive branch and arrows
example: The Great Seal appears on the back of the one-dollar bill

definition: Rules for proper handling and display of the American flag
example: The flag should never touch the ground and is flown at half-staff to honor those who have died

definition: 'The Star-Spangled Banner,' written in 1814, the official song of the United States
example: The National Anthem is played before major sporting events and national ceremonies

definition: Oath of loyalty to the United States and its flag, often recited in schools
example: The Pledge of Allegiance ends with 'with liberty and justice for all'

definition: Japanese attack on the U.S. naval base in Hawaii on December 7, 1941, causing the U.S. to enter WWII
example: President Roosevelt called December 7, 1941 'a date which will live in infamy'

definition: Period of political tension between the U.S. and Soviet Union from the 1940s to 1991
example: The space race between the U.S. and USSR was part of the Cold War

definition: Global war from 1939–1945; the U.S. entered after the attack on Pearl Harbor in 1941
example: D-Day in 1944 was the Allied invasion of Normandy, France that turned the tide of WWII

definition: Global war from 1914–1918; the U.S. entered in 1917 to help the Allies
example: Woodrow Wilson led the U.S. into WWI and proposed the League of Nations

definition: Forced separation of people by race in public places, schools, and transportation
example: Before the Civil Rights Act, many Southern states had segregated schools and lunch counters

definition: Law banning discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, or national origin
example: The Civil Rights Act made it illegal to refuse service to someone based on their race

definition: Civil Rights leader known for nonviolent protest and his 'I Have a Dream' speech
example: MLK led the 1963 March on Washington where he gave his famous speech

definition: Social movement in the 1950s–1960s to end racial segregation and discrimination
example: Rosa Parks and Martin Luther King Jr. were leaders of the Civil Rights Movement

definition: Abolished slavery throughout the United States, ratified in 1865
example: The 13th Amendment permanently ended slavery after the Civil War

definition: 1863 order by Lincoln declaring enslaved people in Confederate states to be free
example: The Emancipation Proclamation was a turning point that made the Civil War about ending slavery

definition: 16th President who led the Union through the Civil War and issued the Emancipation Proclamation
example: Lincoln's Gettysburg Address described government 'of the people, by the people, for the people'

definition: War fought from 1861–1865 between the Union (North) and the Confederacy (South) over slavery
example: Over 600,000 soldiers died in the Civil War, making it the deadliest American conflict

definition: The right of Native American tribes to govern themselves as independent nations
example: Federally recognized tribes can establish their own laws and governments

definition: Areas of land set aside by the U.S. government for Native American tribes
example: Today, federally recognized tribes have sovereignty over their reservation lands

definition: 1830 law that forced Native Americans to relocate west of the Mississippi River
example: President Andrew Jackson signed the Indian Removal Act in 1830

definition: Forced migration of Native Americans westward in the 1830s resulting in thousands of deaths
example: The Cherokee Nation was forced to walk over 1,000 miles, and many died

definition: Prohibits cruel and unusual punishment and excessive bail
example: Torturing a prisoner would violate the 8th Amendment

definition: The right to have an attorney, even if you cannot afford one
example: If you cannot afford a lawyer, the government must provide one for free

definition: Protection against being tried twice for the same crime, guaranteed by the 5th Amendment
example: If found not guilty, you cannot be tried again for the same crime

definition: The presumption that accused persons are innocent until the government proves guilt
example: In the U.S., the prosecution must prove guilt beyond a reasonable doubt

definition: Rights that protect individuals from discrimination and guarantee equal treatment
example: The Civil Rights Act of 1964 banned discrimination based on race, color, or religion

definition: The shared benefit and welfare of the entire community
example: Public schools and fire departments exist for the common good

definition: The idea that citizens give up some freedoms in exchange for government protection of rights
example: We obey traffic laws (a limit on freedom) in exchange for safer roads for everyone

definition: The obligation of citizens to serve on a jury when called upon by a court
example: Jury duty ensures that accused persons are judged by a group of their peers

definition: Tax paid to the federal and state government on earnings from work
example: Americans file income tax returns each year, usually by April 15

definition: System requiring men 18–25 to register in case a military draft is needed
example: Male citizens and residents must register with Selective Service at age 18

definition: A non-citizen who has legal permission to live and work permanently in the U.S.
example: A green card holder is a permanent resident who can apply for citizenship after 5 years

definition: Obligations of citizens to their country, such as voting, jury service, and paying taxes
example: Serving on a jury is a civic duty that helps ensure fair trials

definition: The legal process by which an immigrant becomes a U.S. citizen
example: After five years as a permanent resident, most immigrants can apply for naturalization

definition: A person who is a legal member of a country and has full rights and responsibilities
example: U.S. citizens can vote, run for office, and hold a U.S. passport

definition: The 14th Amendment guarantee that laws apply equally to all people
example: Schools cannot be segregated because equal protection requires equal treatment

definition: The right to fair legal procedures before the government can take away life, liberty, or property
example: You have the right to a lawyer and a fair trial under due process

definition: The right to practice any religion, or no religion, without government interference
example: Americans can worship as Muslims, Christians, Jews, Hindus, or not at all

definition: The right to express opinions without government censorship or retaliation
example: You can criticize government policies without fear of arrest due to freedom of speech

definition: The Senate must approve presidential appointments to courts and Cabinet positions
example: Supreme Court nominees must be confirmed by a Senate vote

definition: The process where Congress formally charges a president or official with wrongdoing
example: The House impeaches and the Senate holds the trial to decide removal

definition: System where each branch of government can limit the power of the other branches
example: The President vetoes laws, Congress overrides vetoes, and courts strike down unconstitutional acts

definition: Federal judges serve until they die, retire, or are removed, ensuring independence
example: Supreme Court justices have lifetime appointments so they can rule without political pressure

definition: The head of the Supreme Court and the federal judiciary
example: John Marshall was one of the most influential Chief Justices in U.S. history

definition: The Supreme Court's power to declare laws unconstitutional
example: In Marbury v. Madison, the Supreme Court established the power of judicial review

definition: The highest court in the U.S., with nine justices and final authority on constitutional questions
example: The Supreme Court's rulings set legal precedents for all lower courts

definition: Limits the President to a maximum of two terms in office
example: FDR served four terms, which led to the 22nd Amendment limiting future presidents to two

definition: The President's power to reject legislation passed by Congress
example: A President can veto a bill they disagree with, sending it back to Congress

definition: Group of department heads who advise the President and manage executive departments
example: The Secretary of State and Secretary of Defense are Cabinet members

definition: Head of the Executive Branch, elected to four-year terms, limited to two terms
example: The President signs bills into law and is commander-in-chief of the military

definition: The building in Washington, D.C. where Congress meets
example: Both the Senate and House of Representatives meet in the Capitol Building

definition: Congress can reverse a presidential veto with a two-thirds vote in both chambers
example: If the President vetoes a bill, Congress can still pass it with enough votes

definition: Lower chamber of Congress with 435 members based on state population, serving 2-year terms
example: California has many more House members than Wyoming because it has more people

definition: Upper chamber of Congress with 100 members, two from each state, serving 6-year terms
example: There are always exactly 100 senators, regardless of state population

definition: The principle that everyone, including government officials, must follow the law
example: Even the President must obey the law — no one is above it

definition: Division of government into three branches: legislative, executive, and judicial
example: Congress makes laws, the President enforces them, and courts interpret them

definition: Division of power between the national government and state governments
example: Education is mainly controlled by states, while national defense is federal

definition: A system where citizens elect representatives to govern on their behalf
example: The U.S. is a democratic republic — citizens vote for senators and representatives

definition: Lowered the voting age from 21 to 18, ratified in 1971
example: Young people who served in Vietnam pushed for the 26th Amendment

definition: 1965 federal law that eliminated literacy tests and other barriers to voting
example: The Voting Rights Act was passed during the Civil Rights Movement to protect African American voters

definition: Granted women the right to vote, ratified in 1920
example: Susan B. Anthony was a key leader in the fight that led to the 19th Amendment

definition: Prohibited voting discrimination based on race, ratified in 1870
example: The 15th Amendment gave African American men the right to vote after the Civil War

definition: Protects against unreasonable searches and seizures by the government
example: Police generally need a warrant to search your home under the Fourth Amendment

definition: Protects the right of the people to keep and bear arms
example: The Second Amendment has been the subject of many Supreme Court decisions

definition: Freedoms guaranteed by law that protect individuals from government overreach
example: Free speech and the right to a fair trial are civil liberties protected by the Constitution

definition: Protects freedom of speech, religion, press, assembly, and petition
example: The First Amendment allows people to criticize the government without being arrested

definition: War fought from 1775–1783 in which the American colonies won independence from Britain
example: George Washington commanded the Continental Army during the Revolutionary War

definition: National holiday on July 4th celebrating the signing of the Declaration of Independence
example: Americans celebrate Independence Day with fireworks and parades

definition: Founding Father and primary author of the Declaration of Independence
example: Jefferson declared 'all men are created equal' in the Declaration

definition: Document adopted on July 4, 1776 declaring the colonies' independence from Britain
example: Thomas Jefferson wrote most of the Declaration of Independence

definition: The first governing document of the U.S., replaced by the Constitution because it was too weak
example: Under the Articles, Congress had no power to levy taxes or enforce laws

definition: The process of formal state approval required for the Constitution to take effect
example: The Constitution was ratified by nine states in 1788 before it could go into effect

definition: The first ten amendments to the Constitution, protecting fundamental individual freedoms
example: The Bill of Rights guarantees freedom of speech, religion, and the right to a fair trial

definition: Called the 'Father of the Constitution' for his central role in drafting it
example: Madison came prepared with the Virginia Plan, which formed the basis of the Constitution

definition: Meeting of 55 delegates in Philadelphia in 1787 to draft the U.S. Constitution
example: James Madison and Benjamin Franklin were key delegates at the Constitutional Convention

definition: Historic bell in Philadelphia symbolizing American independence
example: The Liberty Bell is displayed at Independence Hall in Philadelphia

definition: Monument in New York Harbor symbolizing freedom and opportunity
example: The Statue of Liberty was a gift from France to the United States

definition: National bird symbolizing strength, courage, and independence
example: The Bald Eagle appears on the Great Seal of the United States

definition: National flag with 13 stripes and 50 stars
example: The 13 stripes represent the original colonies and stars represent current states

definition: Power of courts to declare laws unconstitutional
example: The Supreme Court used judicial review to overturn segregation laws

definition: Highest court with nine justices who interpret the Constitution
example: Supreme Court decisions set legal precedents for the entire nation

definition: Supreme Court and federal courts that interpret laws
example: The Supreme Court can declare laws unconstitutional

definition: President's power to reject legislation passed by Congress
example: Congress can override a presidential veto with a two-thirds majority vote

definition: Led by President, enforces laws and manages government
example: The President commands the military and appoints cabinet members

definition: Lower chamber with 435 members based on state population
example: Larger states like California have more Representatives than smaller states

definition: Upper chamber of Congress with 100 members (2 from each state)
example: Each state has two Senators serving six-year terms

definition: Congress (Senate and House) that makes federal laws
example: The Legislative Branch passes laws that affect the entire nation

definition: Commander of Continental Army and first President of the United States
example: George Washington led the American forces to victory against the British

definition: 1773 protest where colonists dumped British tea into Boston Harbor
example: The Boston Tea Party was a response to taxes imposed without colonial representation

definition: Conflict from 1775-1783 resulting in American independence from Britain
example: George Washington commanded the Continental Army during the Revolutionary War

definition: Document adopted July 4, 1776, declaring American independence from Britain
example: Thomas Jefferson wrote the Declaration stating that all men are created equal

definition: First ten amendments protecting fundamental individual freedoms
example: The Bill of Rights includes freedoms of speech, religion, and the right to a fair trial

definition: Process of state approval required for the Constitution to become law
example: The Constitution was ratified by the states in 1788 and went into effect in 1789

definition: Called the 'Father of the Constitution' for his central role in shaping it
example: James Madison came prepared with detailed plans that became the basis for the Constitution

definition: Meeting of delegates in Philadelphia in 1787 to draft the U.S. Constitution
example: The Constitutional Convention brought together leaders like James Madison and Benjamin Franklin
